3. Respondent No.2, the Bank opposed the Rule by filing an affidavit-in opposition controverting the statement made in the writ petition contending inter alia, that the Bank filed Money Decree Execution Case No. 08 of 1995 along with an application for condensation of delay as per provision of the Limitation Act and the Ain. Therefore, execution proceeding as well as the order for issuing warrant of arrest is lawful and the Rule is thus, liable to be discharged. 

 4. Mr. Md. Hadayet Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the suit was decreed on 19-9-1991 and the execution case for execution of the decree was filed firstly on 16-7-1995 and, as such, the execution case having been filed beyond the period of 3 years as required under Article 182 of the Limitation act is barred by limitation. He lastly submits that the execution case being barred by limitation the entire proceeding of the Money Decree Execution Case is liable to be declared to be without lawful authority. 

 5. Mr. ASM Abdul Razzaque, the learned Advocate for the Bank submits that from the record of Money Decree Execution Case No. 08 of 1995 it is evident that the execution case has been filed along with an application for condonation of delay and, as such, it is to be presumed that the said application is allowed as the Adalat proceeded with the execution case and as such, the execution case is not barred by limitation and therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged.
